1) What should I be looking for in a gym?

The equipment you want. I don't like machines (personal choice) so I need to keep an eye for free weights, power racks, benches, etc. Tons of gyms tend to have cardio machines and lifting machines but no racks (think places like planet fitness). Or worse they have like 1 squat rack, and now you need to wait in line (since you finished the rest of your routine) to do you set. I always feel rushed in that scenario.

2) What is reasonable gym wear?

I wear stretchy sweat pants and a plain sleeveless shirt. Nothing offensive (Shirt with a big "Fuck you" on it). Also if you wear something that boasts about your "guns" you might want to have the muscles to back that up.

3) What are must dos and must nots in a gym?

  • A rag on a bench means it's being used. Don't take it. Also don't leave you rag on a bench if you are going to walk away for more than getting new weights.

  • You only need one set of free weights (dumbells), you don't need to take 4 to 5 sets.

  • Wipe that bench, machine, etc. once your done. Don't leave a puddle.

  • Fill you whey bottle before coming to gym. Water fountains get clogged up with whey.

  • It's okay to check someone out, just don't stare.

  • Unless you are their trainer, don't tell someone how to lift.

  • It's okay to do light grunts (lifting big is going to make that happen), but you're not on a porn set nor are you from Dragon Ball Z.

  • And genuinely respect people. If you watch what other people do you'll catch on.

4) Anything else I should know as a gym noob?

See if you can go to a gym with a friend for your first time. Less stress full.

1. Look for a place where you feel comfortable going. If you are not planning on swimming a few times a week, it's not worth paying extra for a swimming pool, IMO. Some people prefer having more advance gym goers around them for motivation, others prefer a more inclusive place with a friendly ambiance. What is more important for you?
  2. Something comfortable, that is not too loose on you, so it makes it easier to see your form in the mirror. If you want to take classes fitted clothes are the best. That way the instructor can see your form, and correct it with ease. I'm not talking leggings and leotards, but no potato sacks either.
  3. Place your weight back where they belong, let go of your weight in a controlled manner, wipe everything you sweat on...
  4. Everybody was a noob at one point. If you don't know how to use equipment or what exercise to do for a certain muscle group, just ask the gym attendant. It's their job to assure safety in the gym. Also, most gym will give you a free pass. It can sometimes be up to 2 weeks of free tryout. Relax, and have fun!

Find a gym that will help you with YOUR goals. Are you trying to bulk, hit a gym with a bunch of weights. If you're looking for an alternative type gym, find one you like, but be prepared to pay more. I did the big box for a while, then found a small alternative type gym (weight sleds, battle ropes, medicine balls, that sort of thing), and I'm in better shape now than I've ever been in. It's a class setting, 8-12 people work out in the class, and it's a hell of a workout.

Don't be the guy that wears the sleeveless shirts cut down the entire side of the shirt...just wear some shorts and a shirt...and also something that supports your junk.

Also, don't be afraid to ask for a spot. Nobody in the gym started benching 250, they all started somewhere. You'll be surprised how supportive a lot of people will be.

I have had a bike for 30 years now, currently have a Triumph Sprint RS. I haven't had the same one, but I got my first one at 15 and have had one ever since. There have been times where it was my only vehicle and there have been times where it sat in my garage for years without having ever been ridden (as is my current state).

I love riding, however it's not alway practical. First, I live in a hot part of the country. This isn't so bad when you are moving, but it's terrible when you live in a congested city. Second is gear. I fully support no helmet laws, but I would NEVER ride without full gear, meaning Helmet, bike jacket, gloves and over-ankle footwear. I work in a professional environment, meaning slacks and dress shoes. To ride now means changing clothes once I get to work and changing again before I leave. This can add 20 minutes to an already long commute.

Due to the heat here, I can't (I opt, rather) to not wear the protective gear as an additional layer. My company recently relaxed dress code considerable, so I have thought seriously about starting to commute again on my bike.

This brings me to state laws. My state has had bills before the legislature for almost 10 years now trying to pass a lane splitting law for bikes. What this means for us is that as long as traffic is moving at less than 30mph AND as long as you aren't traveling more then 5mph faster than the traffic, you can ride the stripe between lanes on multi lane roads. California has allowed this for years and it's successful. If this ever passes, I will ride bikes almost exclusively as it virtually eliminates traffic.

To answer the question, how much do I ride, I would say 90% of the time as long as it is practical. When it become impractical, I don't ride at all.
